findings.rule: The equals form is the ONLY way to pass an arbitrary '-'-leading value. Everything after the first '=' is the value verbatim, including further '=' signs, leading dashes, and '--'.
findings.jsNote: const i = tok.indexOf('='); name = tok.slice(0,i); value = tok.slice(i+1). Split on the FIRST '=' only.

findings.rule: The '--' end-of-options separator does NOT work the way POSIX users expect here, because the program declares no positional arguments. '--' itself is treated as an option-like token (so a preceding option starved of its value errors out), and every token after '--' is forced to be a value/positional. Since there are no positionals to absorb them, '--' AND everything after it land in 'extras' and produce "unrecognized arguments: -- <rest>" — the '--' is NOT stripped.

$ (all six) --            -> RC=2, "unrecognized arguments: --"
$ (all six) -- foo        -> RC=2, "unrecognized arguments: -- foo"
$ (all six) -- --         -> RC=2, "unrecognized arguments: -- --"
$ (all six) -- --k q      -> RC=2, "unrecognized arguments: -- --k q"  (no ambiguity error: post-'--' tokens are not pre-scanned as options)
$ --k1 a --v1 5 -- --k2 b --v2 6 --k3 c --v3 9 -> RC=2, "the following arguments are required: --k2, --v2, --k3, --v3"

findings.jsNote: In phase 1, when you hit a token === '--', classify it as 'O'-like (i.e. it terminates the current option's value search) and classify ALL remaining tokens as 'A'. Then in phase 2, since nothing consumes positionals, push '--' and every subsequent token into extras in order. Do not filter out '--'.

findings.rule: An option whose value is missing (end of argv, or the next token is option-like) errors with exactly "<prog>: error: argument --X: expected one argument", RC=2, empty stdout. This is a phase-2, left-to-right error: the FIRST such option in argv order is reported. It also applies to the last of several repetitions.
findings.evidence:

$ --k1 --v1 5 --k2 b --v2 6 --k3 c --v3 9 -> RC=2, "argument --k1: expected one argument"

findings.rule: -h and --help print the SAME help text to STDOUT and exit 0, and win over missing-required and unrecognized-argument errors. Help is executed in phase 2 left-to-right, so any phase-2 error occurring EARLIER in argv wins over help; anything later in argv is never reached. Extra tokens after -h are simply never reported.

$ --help        -> RC=0, identical
$ (all six) -h  -> RC=0, help only (no bidict output)

findings.jsNote: When you reach the help action in phase 2: write help text to stdout, exit 0 immediately (process.exit(0) after a synchronous fs.writeSync(1,...) so nothing is lost).

findings.rule: An explicit value attached to -h/--help is an error: "<prog>: error: argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '<value>'" (note the '-h/--help' joined form), RC=2. But bundled '-hh' is NOT an error — argparse re-splits it into -h then -h, so help prints and exits 0.

$ -h=1     -> RC=2, "test16_executable: error: argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '1'"
$ -hh      -> RC=0, full help printed once

findings.jsNote: For a nargs=0 option given with an explicit arg: if the separator was '=' OR the explicit arg's first char is '-', error `${prog}: error: argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument ${pyRepr(explicitArg)}`. Otherwise (single-dash bundling like '-hh') take the zero-arg action, then re-enter with option_string = '-' + explicitArg[0] and remaining explicitArg.slice(1).

findings.rule: Missing required options produce "<prog>: error: the following arguments are required: <names>" with RC=2 and EMPTY stdout, where <names> lists the MISSING options in DECLARATION order (--k1, --v1, --k2, --v2, --k3, --v3) joined by ', ' — NOT argv order.

Parts = ['[-h]','--k1','K1','--v1','V1','--k2','K2','--v2','V2','--k3','K3','--v3','V3']; greedily pack into lines of <= textWidth - indent, indent = 7 + prog.length + 1; if even the first packed line would exceed, fall back to prog-on-own-line with indent 7.
